participation.context: Stood, wrote nothing, and left the question at home.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Read the long gospel, refused haste, and looked at nobody.
participation.name: Master Josias Thwaite

participation.context: Kept the aisle from being trimmed, and kept it from becoming a report.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Said the ledge was bare, and that there was no bread and no cup.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

relations.quote: I have not looked at you, and I am not about to begin.

story.body: You heard the long gospel and kept the pen off your knee. You did not bring the morning's question into the aisle. You took no bread and no cup, because none was offered.

relations.quote: I have not looked at you, and I am not about to begin.

title: Stood for the long gospel in black

participation.context: Stood, added nothing, and kept the afternoon quiet.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Kept the evening to the prayer.
participation.name: Master Josias Thwaite

participation.context: Refused a dressing-up and a new matter.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Said the ledge was still bare.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

relations.quote: I did not bring the house out a second time to hear a new matter.

story.body: You heard the prayer and refused a new matter. You went to leave when he finished, with the afternoon still quiet.

relations.quote: I did not bring the house out a second time to hear a new matter.
